additional_native_flow_verifications.scope: Original achievement/category claim UI gates, typed senders, native list add/contains, pooled-list cleanup and profile query/caller in both clients. Dictionary presence/get, allocation, repeated-field copying, pool callbacks, transport and final UI service use controlled fixtures. No IFix, native hash-table internals, error branches, live server eligibility or network interoperability is claimed.

Original activity claim sender and one globally unique caller execute in both builds, covering activity/watcher field roles, uint32 bits, independent readonly checks and missing lookup suppression. Allocation, lookup data, readonly status and transport are controlled fixtures. Other unique caller contexts are statically checked; real claim eligibility, IFix and live networking are not exercised.

Original unique caller and typed request sender execute with different cached chapter IDs, exact gate values and readonly fixtures in both builds. Allocation, readonly status and transport use controlled fixtures; IFix and live coop task cancellation are not exercised.

Revalidates six existing supplied-NT or native-backed request names, native empty schemas and original current CmdId getters for requests and their already-bound replies. Corrects three stale active bindings while enabling three missing ones. This does not add recovered aliases or establish live feature behavior. Existing handler behavior is retained, including empty success replies for unimplemented map content.

Original home-manager wrapper and request sender in both builds, target uint32 bits, readonly fixture and exact ordering of the post-send flag write. Allocation, readonly state and transport use controlled fixtures. Global CFG uniqueness, response pairing by transaction, flag business meaning, IFix and live realm switching are not claimed.

Original three typed uint32/bool senders and current native CmdId getters. Both invitation dispatchers are statically matched with exact sender call positions and an independently named dungeon branch. Allocation, readonly flags and transport are fixtures. Dispatcher execution, request/response pairing, real invitation acceptance and live networking are not exercised; server bindings remain withheld.

Original native mail senders, single/favorite deletion, single and batch attachment claim loops, read-before-claim sequence, list add/clear and attachment/special-row predicates are executed in both builds. Typed repeated-field clear/copy, row lookup, allocation, capacity checks, read-cache pre-send callback and transport use controlled fixtures. IFix, error/overflow branches, over-capacity warnings and live network sessions are not exercised. No request/response transaction is inferred solely from sender shape.

Original match/draft sender instructions, post-send branches and repeated-ID copy/add loops execute in both builds; current CmdId getters execute. Config ID decoding executes with synthetic substitution tables and is not a wire mask. Allocation, readonly flags, typed collection operations, config lookup, local callback lookup/action and transport use fixtures. Callback business identities, caller execution, IFix replacement paths, complete request/reply transactions and live networking are outside scope.

Original MP-play invitation/check request bodies and CmdId getters execute in both builds. Declared MP-play field names distinguish same-shaped scene-play counterparts; full native ABI/callee identities and all module senders are checked. Allocation, readonly results, cached state, post-send collection cleanup and transport use fixtures. Response schemas are independent naming controls, not captured transaction proof. IFix and live networking are outside scope.

Original two-word sender bodies, scene invitation sender and current CmdId getters execute in both builds. Exact argument moves and corresponding field-store instructions disambiguate reordered uint32 fields. The scene invitation uses its independently verified owner-check companion and the same cached skip-match byte. Allocation, independent readonly states, the post-send cleanup and transport are fixtures; IFix is disabled. Caller execution, business-domain validation, paired responses and live networking are not exercised; high-bit values only test serialization bit preservation.

Original empty request sender, both confirmation-gated team deletion senders, selected-index resolver and ordinary list getter in both builds. Allocation, readonly flags, synthetic team lists, transport and the final dialog action use controlled fixtures. Out-of-range index error paths, IFix and live network sessions are not exercised.

Original full multiplayer-lobby initializer, empty sender and native ordinary-list clear execute in both clients. UI services, metadata globals, delegate/packet allocation, widget callback and transport use controlled fixtures. Matching fixture call order is supporting flow evidence, not an independent proof of every UI callee identity. IFix, null/error branches, lobby refresh timing and live networking are not exercised.

Original request/reply bodies, changed-card caller, nonnull string check, half-second request throttle and selected music config decoder. Allocator, readonly state, card membership, engine clock, UI/coroutine services and transport are controlled fixtures; the config substitution table is synthetic. Null string throwing, IFix replacement branches and live Android/network transactions are outside this verification.

Original reply error/success branches in both clients and the current CmdId getter execute. The semantic name uses bidirectionally unique typed consumers within independently paired modules and an independently verified request. Error UI and IFix-disabled flags are fixtures. The frozen public baseline remains unchanged; only the documented weaker alias is replaced. No live pending-request transaction or recovered original 7.2 source spelling is claimed.

Original primitive/empty request senders and current CmdId getters execute. Caller identity uses globally unique normalized bodies, exact sender call positions and at least three independently supported other calls. Allocation, per-field readonly results, cached scene-play bool and transport are fixtures; IFix is disabled. Caller execution, request/response transactions, server business behavior and live networking are not exercised. Unknown field roles remain unnamed; no mask or server binding is inferred from sender shape alone.

Original retcode branches and two native event producers execute in both builds, plus current CmdId getters. Named reply identities use complete paired-module consumer sets, full native ABI, closed field-type compatibility, independently supported callees/events and reverse conflict checks. Error/UI services, boxing, event construction and dispatch are fixtures; IFix is disabled. Extra unconsumed field names and live request/response transactions are not inferred.

Original typed request senders in both builds and native CmdId getters. Unique caller contexts are checked statically. Allocation, readonly flags, home-state return four and transport are controlled fixtures. The home edit warning branch and its unresolved getter, IFix, server reward/business behavior, home scene reply pairing and live networking are not exercised.

Original request senders, both realm confirmation callbacks and tower reply success/error consumer execute in both builds. Allocation, readonly flags, coroutine service and transport use fixtures. The response buff-ID name uses the matched reference shape and shared request symbol; no native reply buff-ID consumption, live request/response transaction, IFix or live game session is claimed.

Both retained trial-avatar interfaces and original sender execute in both builds, covering zero-index suppression, uint32 index bits and readonly fixtures. Allocation, readonly status and transport are controlled fixtures; IFix and real reward eligibility/granting are not exercised.
